source.original_text:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel sigma algebra, including dimension zero. Let V:E->R, alpha,beta>=0 and eta in R. Assume alpha>0, alpha<=beta, V is C2, alpha||v||^2<=D2V(x)[v,v]<=beta||v||^2 for every x,v in E, eta>0 and beta*eta<=1.
For y,r in E put c=y-eta grad V(r), h_r(x)=grad V(x)-grad V(r), R(x,p)=(x,-p),
Phi_(y,r,u)(x,p)=(c+cos(u)(x-c)+sqrt(eta)sin(u)p, -sin(u)/sqrt(eta)(x-c)+cos(u)p),
S_r(x,p)=(x,p-(2<p,h_r(x)>/||h_r(x)||^2)h_r(x)). Real division by zero is zero, so a zero normal gives the identity bounce. Let ell=volume_E tensor volume_E, with canonical Hilbert-space Lebesgue measure.
For every integer n>=0 and horizon T>=0, let Delta_n(T) consist of real tuples 0<t_0<...<t_(n-1)<T. Equivalently, prepending 0 produces a strictly increasing tuple and every entry is less than T. Let Prefix_n(T) be this subtype and m_n,T the comap of Lebesgue measure on R^n under its inclusion. This is unnormalized simplex volume. For n=0 the tuple is empty and its zero-dimensional volume is one; for T=0 and n>0 the subtype is empty.
Write q_0=0 and q_(j+1)=t_j. Starting at z_0=z, define z_(j+1)=S_r(Phi_(y,r,t_j-q_j)(z_j)) for 0<=j<n. Define records K_j=(q_j,z_j), each embedded in the live branch of (R_nonnegative x (E x E)) plus a cemetery symbol. For a general history of n+1 such records, the path reconstruction Psi at s in [0,T] starts from z and visits records in increasing index order: a live record (a,w) replaces the accumulator by Phi_(y,r,s-a)(w) exactly when a<=s; future records and cemetery records leave it unchanged. Here s-a is nonnegative subtraction. Define Gamma_(y,r,z,t)=Psi(K), the actual finite prescribed path; thus its value at an event is the post-bounce value. Let A_(y,r)(z,t)=Gamma_(y,r,z,t)(T).
Define the actual positive-part event rate lambda_r(x,p)=sqrt(eta) max(0,<p,grad V(x)-grad V(r)>), and the target energy U_y(x,p)=V(x)+||x-y||^2/(2 eta)+||p||^2/2. The rate after momentum reversal is lambda_r(R(x,p)); it is evaluated on the same trajectory, not on a reversed-time trajectory.
For every y,r,z,n,T,t as above, extend the actual prescribed path to real s by gamma(s)=Gamma(min(max(s,0),T)), with the argument understood as the nonnegative closed-interval subtype. Put A=Gamma(T), Iplus=integral from 0 to T of lambda_r(gamma(s)) ds, and Iminus=integral from 0 to T of lambda_r(R(gamma(s))) ds, both with real Lebesgue measure. Both integrands are interval integrable. The exact identities are
U_y(A)-U_y(z)=Iplus-Iminus,
exp(-U_y(z)) exp(-Iplus)=exp(-U_y(A)) exp(-Iminus).
All finite event counts n>=0, horizons T>=0, rank-zero spaces and zero reflection normals are included. No positive jump-rate condition is imposed on the prescribed tuple. No measurability, integrability, energy identity or normalizing-constant premise is added to the six source assumptions. The simplex measure m is retained to preserve the existing path interface but is not used by these two scalar identities. The weights here are unnormalized; a common Gibbs normalizer would cancel but existence of the normalized stationary law is a separate obligation.
This is the actual finite prescribed-path energy and Gibbs/survival identity in the Appendix A.1 reversal proof. It does not assert reversed-event density matching, pointwise time reversal at right-continuous jump values, weighted sector preservation, stationary averaging or invariant probability laws, restart/Markovness, hypocoercivity, implementation errors, expected oracle cost, main sampling results or actual-input composition.

{E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    {V : E → ℝ} {α β : ℝ≥0} {η : ℝ}
    (hα : 0 < (α : ℝ)) (hαβ : α ≤ β) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E,
      (α : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ (β : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hβη : (β : ℝ) * η ≤ 1) :
    let c : E → E → E := fun y xRef => y - η • gradient V xRef
    let Φ : E → E → ℝ → (E × E) → (E × E) := fun y xRef t z =>
      (c y xRef + Real.cos t • (z.1 - c y xRef) +
          (Real.sqrt η * Real.sin t) • z.2,
       (-Real.sin t / Real.sqrt η) • (z.1 - c y xRef) + Real.cos t • z.2)
    let S : E → (E × E) → (E × E) := fun xRef z =>
      (z.1, z.2 - (2 * inner ℝ z.2 (gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef) /
        ‖gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef‖ ^ 2) • (gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef))
    let Rec := (ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit
    let Hist : ℕ → Type _ := fun n => Fin (n + 1) → Rec
    let Δ : (n : ℕ) → ℝ≥0 → Set (Fin n → ℝ) := fun n T =>
      {t | StrictMono (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t) ∧ ∀ i, t i < (T : ℝ)}
    let Prefix : (n : ℕ) → ℝ≥0 → Type := fun n T => {t : Fin n → ℝ // t ∈ Δ n T}
    let m : (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) → Measure (Prefix n T) := fun n T =>
      Measure.comap (fun t : Prefix n T => t.val) (volume : Measure (Fin n → ℝ))
    let zAt : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
        Prefix n T → Fin (n + 1) → (E × E) := fun y xRef z₀ n T t =>
      Fin.induction z₀ (fun i z =>
        S xRef (Φ y xRef (t.val i - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i.castSucc) z))
    let K : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
        Prefix n T → Hist n := fun y xRef z₀ n T t j =>
      Sum.inl (Real.toNNReal ((Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) j), zAt y xRef z₀ n T t j)
    let Path : ℝ≥0 → Type _ := fun T => {s : ℝ≥0 // s ≤ T} → E × E
    let Ψ : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) → Hist n → Path T :=
      fun y xRef z₀ n T h s =>
        Fin.foldl (n + 1) (fun z j => (h j).elim
          (fun a => if a.1 ≤ s.val then Φ y xRef ((s.val - a.1 : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) a.2 else z)
          (fun _ => z)) z₀
    let Γ : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) → Prefix n T → Path T :=
      fun y xRef z₀ n T t => Ψ y xRef z₀ n T (K y xRef z₀ n T t)
    let R : E × E → E × E := fun z => (z.1, -z.2)
    let rate : E → E × E → ℝ := fun r z =>
      Real.sqrt η * max 0 (inner ℝ z.2 (gradient V z.1 - gradient V r))
    let U : E → E × E → ℝ := fun y z =>
      V z.1 + ‖z.1 - y‖ ^ 2 / (2 * η) + ‖z.2‖ ^ 2 / 2
    ∀ y r : E, ∀ z : E × E, ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ T : ℝ≥0, ∀ t : Prefix n T,
      let gamma : ℝ → E × E := fun s =>
        Γ y r z n T t ⟨min (Real.toNNReal s) T, min_le_right _ _⟩
      let A : E × E := Γ y r z n T t ⟨T, le_rfl⟩
      let Iplus : ℝ := ∫ s in (0 : ℝ)..(T : ℝ), rate r (gamma s)
      let Iminus : ℝ := ∫ s in (0 : ℝ)..(T : ℝ), rate r (R (gamma s))
      IntervalIntegrable (fun s => rate r (gamma s)) volume 0 (T : ℝ) ∧
      IntervalIntegrable (fun s => rate r (R (gamma s))) volume 0 (T : ℝ) ∧
      U y A - U y z = Iplus - Iminus ∧
      Real.exp (-U y z) * Real.exp (-Iplus) = Real.exp (-U y A) * Real.exp (-Iminus)
decoder_context: gradient and fderiv denote real Hilbert gradient and Frechet derivative; the space is finite-dimensional with Borel structure.
Fin n indexes n coordinates from zero. Fin.cons prepends, Fin.induction is finite recursion, and Fin.foldl visits records in increasing index order.

Real division by zero equals zero. Real.toNNReal is the nonnegative part. Subtraction in the nonnegative reals is truncated at zero. Sum.inl is the live-record constructor; Unit is the cemetery branch.
The path domain is the nonnegative closed-interval subtype. Measure.comap uses the exact unnormalized subtype measure. volume on the real line is Lebesgue measure.

IntervalIntegrable f volume a b states integrability on both oriented interval restrictions; the interval integral uses the standard signed orientation. Real.exp is the real exponential. Unused let definitions do not introduce theorem hypotheses.

private theorem actual_arc_energy
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    {V : E → ℝ} {α β : ℝ≥0} {η : ℝ}
    (hα : 0 < (α : ℝ)) (hαβ : α ≤ β) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E,
      (α : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ (β : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hβη : (β : ℝ) * η ≤ 1) :
    let c : E → E → E := fun y r => y - η • gradient V r
    let Φ : E → E → ℝ → (E × E) → (E × E) := fun y r t z =>
      (c y r + Real.cos t • (z.1 - c y r) +
          (Real.sqrt η * Real.sin t) • z.2,
       (-Real.sin t / Real.sqrt η) • (z.1 - c y r) + Real.cos t • z.2)
    let R : E × E → E × E := fun z => (z.1, -z.2)
    let rate : E → E × E → ℝ := fun r z =>
      Real.sqrt η * max 0 (inner ℝ z.2 (gradient V z.1 - gradient V r))
    let U : E → E × E → ℝ := fun y z =>
      V z.1 + ‖z.1 - y‖ ^ 2 / (2 * η) + ‖z.2‖ ^ 2 / 2
    ∀ y r : E, ∀ z : E × E,
      (∀ s : ℝ, HasDerivAt (fun t => U y (Φ y r t z))
        (rate r (Φ y r s z) - rate r (R (Φ y r s z))) s) ∧
      (∀ a b : ℝ,
        IntervalIntegrable (fun s => rate r (Φ y r s z)) volume a b ∧
        IntervalIntegrable (fun s => rate r (R (Φ y r s z))) volume a b ∧
        U y (Φ y r b z) - U y (Φ y r a z) =
          (∫ s in a..b, rate r (Φ y r s z)) -
          (∫ s in a..b, rate r (R (Φ y r s z)))) := by
  intro c Φ R rate U y r z
  letI : CompleteSpace E := FiniteDimensional.complete ℝ E
  have hf := AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.ActualHarmonicFlow.actual_harmonic_flow_laws
    hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη
  rcases hf with ⟨hc, _, _, _, _, ho, _⟩
  have hb := AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.ActualBounceRate.actual_bounce_rate_energy_laws
    hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη
  have hrate : Continuous (fun q : E × (E × E) => rate q.1 q.2) := hb.2.1
  have hphi : Continuous (fun t => Φ y r t z) :=
    hc.comp ((continuous_const (y := (y,r))).prodMk
      (continuous_id.prodMk (continuous_const (y := z))))
  have hp : Continuous (fun t => rate r (Φ y r t z)) :=
    hrate.comp (continuous_const.prodMk hphi)
  have hm : Continuous (fun t => rate r (R (Φ y r t z))) :=
    hrate.comp (continuous_const.prodMk (hphi.fst.prodMk hphi.snd.neg))
  have hdiff (q : E × E) : rate r q - rate r (R q) =
      Real.sqrt η * inner ℝ q.2 (gradient V q.1 - gradient V r) := by
    dsimp [rate, R]
    rw [inner_neg_left]
    by_cases h : 0 ≤ inner ℝ q.2 (gradient V q.1 - gradient V r)
    · rw [max_eq_right h, max_eq_left (neg_nonpos.mpr h)]
      ring
    · rw [max_eq_left (le_of_not_ge h), max_eq_right (neg_nonneg.mpr (le_of_not_ge h))]
      ring
  have hd (s : ℝ) : HasDerivAt (fun t => U y (Φ y r t z))
      (rate r (Φ y r s z) - rate r (R (Φ y r s z))) s := by
    obtain ⟨hx, hv⟩ := ho y r s z
    have hx' : HasDerivAt (fun t => (Φ y r t z).1) (Real.sqrt η • (Φ y r s z).2) s := hx
    have hv' : HasDerivAt (fun t => (Φ y r t z).2)
        (-(Real.sqrt η)⁻¹ • ((Φ y r s z).1 - y) - Real.sqrt η • gradient V r) s := hv
    have hVd := ((hV.differentiable (by norm_num)).differentiableAt.hasGradientAt.hasFDerivAt).comp_hasDerivAt s hx'
    have hd0 := (hVd.add ((hx'.sub_const y).norm_sq.div_const (2 * η))).add
      (hv'.norm_sq.div_const 2)
    apply hd0.congr_deriv
    rw [hdiff]
    simp only [InnerProductSpace.toDual_apply_apply, real_inner_smul_right, real_inner_smul_left,
      inner_sub_right, inner_sub_left, real_inner_comm]
    have hs : (Real.sqrt η) ^ 2 = η := Real.sq_sqrt hη.le
    have hs0 : Real.sqrt η ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt (Real.sqrt_pos.mpr hη)
    field_simp [hs0, hη.ne']
    simp only [hs]
    ring
  refine ⟨hd, ?_⟩
  intro a b
  have hi : IntervalIntegrable (fun s => rate r (Φ y r s z)) volume a b := hp.intervalIntegrable a b
  have hj : IntervalIntegrable (fun s => rate r (R (Φ y r s z))) volume a b := hm.intervalIntegrable a b
  refine ⟨hi, hj, ?_⟩
  rw [← intervalIntegral.integral_sub hi hj]
  exact (intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt (fun s _ => hd s) (hi.sub hj)).symm


/-- Integrable adjacent differences telescope across an energy grid. The
    pointwise path may jump; only endpoint energies need to match. -/
private theorem finite_energy_balance (n : ℕ) (a u : Fin (n+1) → ℝ)
    (f g : ℝ → ℝ)
    (hf : ∀ j : Fin n, IntervalIntegrable f volume (a j.castSucc) (a j.succ))
    (hg : ∀ j : Fin n, IntervalIntegrable g volume (a j.castSucc) (a j.succ))
    (hstep : ∀ j : Fin n,
      (∫ s in a j.castSucc..a j.succ, f s) -
        (∫ s in a j.castSucc..a j.succ, g s) = u j.succ - u j.castSucc) :
    IntervalIntegrable f volume (a 0) (a (Fin.last n)) ∧
    IntervalIntegrable g volume (a 0) (a (Fin.last n)) ∧
    u (Fin.last n) - u 0 =
      (∫ s in a 0..a (Fin.last n), f s) -
        (∫ s in a 0..a (Fin.last n), g s) := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
    have hh := ih (fun i => a i.castSucc) (fun i => u i.castSucc)
      (fun j => hf j.castSucc) (fun j => hg j.castSucc)
      (fun j => by simpa only [Fin.succ_castSucc] using hstep j.castSucc)
    have hfl := hf (Fin.last n)
    have hgl := hg (Fin.last n)
    have hs := hstep (Fin.last n)
    refine ⟨hh.1.trans hfl, hh.2.1.trans hgl, ?_⟩
    have hfi := intervalIntegral.integral_add_adjacent_intervals hh.1 hfl
    have hgi := intervalIntegral.integral_add_adjacent_intervals hh.2.1 hgl
    simp only [Fin.succ_last, Fin.castSucc_zero] at hh hs hfi hgi
    linarith [hh.2.2]


open Set

private def actual_prescribed_gibbs_survival_statement
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    {V : E → ℝ} {α β : ℝ≥0} {η : ℝ}
    (hα : 0 < (α : ℝ)) (hαβ : α ≤ β) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E,
      (α : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ (β : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hβη : (β : ℝ) * η ≤ 1) : Prop := by
  classical
  exact
    let c : E → E → E := fun y xRef => y - η • gradient V xRef
    let Φ : E → E → ℝ → (E × E) → (E × E) := fun y xRef t z =>
      (c y xRef + Real.cos t • (z.1 - c y xRef) +
          (Real.sqrt η * Real.sin t) • z.2,
       (-Real.sin t / Real.sqrt η) • (z.1 - c y xRef) + Real.cos t • z.2)
    let S : E → (E × E) → (E × E) := fun xRef z =>
      (z.1, z.2 - (2 * inner ℝ z.2 (gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef) /
        ‖gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef‖ ^ 2) • (gradient V z.1 - gradient V xRef))
    let Rec := (ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit
    let Hist : ℕ → Type _ := fun n => Fin (n + 1) → Rec
    let Δ : (n : ℕ) → ℝ≥0 → Set (Fin n → ℝ) := fun n T =>
      {t | StrictMono (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) t) ∧ ∀ i, t i < (T : ℝ)}
    let Prefix : (n : ℕ) → ℝ≥0 → Type := fun n T => {t : Fin n → ℝ // t ∈ Δ n T}
    let m : (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) → Measure (Prefix n T) := fun n T =>
      Measure.comap (fun t : Prefix n T => t.val) (volume : Measure (Fin n → ℝ))
    let zAt : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
        Prefix n T → Fin (n + 1) → (E × E) := fun y xRef z₀ n T t =>
      Fin.induction z₀ (fun i z =>
        S xRef (Φ y xRef (t.val i - (Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) i.castSucc) z))
    let K : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) →
        Prefix n T → Hist n := fun y xRef z₀ n T t j =>
      Sum.inl (Real.toNNReal ((Fin.cons (0 : ℝ) (t.val : Fin n → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) j), zAt y xRef z₀ n T t j)
    let Path : ℝ≥0 → Type _ := fun T => {s : ℝ≥0 // s ≤ T} → E × E
    let Ψ : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) → Hist n → Path T :=
      fun y xRef z₀ n T h s =>
        Fin.foldl (n + 1) (fun z j => (h j).elim
          (fun a => if a.1 ≤ s.val then Φ y xRef ((s.val - a.1 : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) a.2 else z)
          (fun _ => z)) z₀
    let Γ : E → E → (E × E) → (n : ℕ) → (T : ℝ≥0) → Prefix n T → Path T :=
      fun y xRef z₀ n T t => Ψ y xRef z₀ n T (K y xRef z₀ n T t)
    let R : E × E → E × E := fun z => (z.1, -z.2)
    let rate : E → E × E → ℝ := fun r z =>
      Real.sqrt η * max 0 (inner ℝ z.2 (gradient V z.1 - gradient V r))
    let U : E → E × E → ℝ := fun y z =>
      V z.1 + ‖z.1 - y‖ ^ 2 / (2 * η) + ‖z.2‖ ^ 2 / 2
    ∀ y r : E, ∀ z : E × E, ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ T : ℝ≥0, ∀ t : Prefix n T,
      let gamma : ℝ → E × E := fun s =>
        Γ y r z n T t ⟨min (Real.toNNReal s) T, min_le_right _ _⟩
      let A : E × E := Γ y r z n T t ⟨T, le_rfl⟩
      let Iplus : ℝ := ∫ s in (0 : ℝ)..(T : ℝ), rate r (gamma s)
      let Iminus : ℝ := ∫ s in (0 : ℝ)..(T : ℝ), rate r (R (gamma s))
      IntervalIntegrable (fun s => rate r (gamma s)) volume 0 (T : ℝ) ∧
      IntervalIntegrable (fun s => rate r (R (gamma s))) volume 0 (T : ℝ) ∧
      U y A - U y z = Iplus - Iminus ∧
      Real.exp (-U y z) * Real.exp (-Iplus) = Real.exp (-U y A) * Real.exp (-Iminus)

/-- Actual finite prescribed target-energy and Gibbs/survival identity under the six source hypotheses. -/
theorem actual_prescribed_gibbs_survival_balance
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    {V : E → ℝ} {α β : ℝ≥0} {η : ℝ}
    (hα : 0 < (α : ℝ)) (hαβ : α ≤ β) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E,
      (α : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ (β : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hβη : (β : ℝ) * η ≤ 1) :
    actual_prescribed_gibbs_survival_statement hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη := by
  unfold actual_prescribed_gibbs_survival_statement
  intro c Φ S Rec Hist Δ Prefix m zAt K Path Ψ Γ R rate U y r z n T t gamma A Iplus Iminus
  let a : Fin (n+1) → ℝ := Fin.cons 0 t.val
  let grid : Fin (n+2) → ℝ := Fin.snoc a (T : ℝ)
  let u : Fin (n+2) → ℝ := Fin.snoc (fun j => U y (zAt y r z n T t j)) (U y A)
  have hflow := AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.ActualHarmonicFlow.actual_harmonic_flow_laws
    hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη
  have hzero : ∀ q : E × E, Φ y r 0 q = q := hflow.2.2.1 y r
  have hb := AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.ActualBounceRate.actual_bounce_rate_energy_laws
    hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη
  have hsU (q : E × E) : U y (S r q) = U y q := by
    have hn := (hb.2.2.2.2.1 (gradient V q.1 - gradient V r) q.2).2.1
    change V q.1 + ‖q.1 - y‖ ^ 2 / (2 * η) + _ / 2 = _
    rw [show ‖(S r q).2‖ = ‖q.2‖ from hn]
  have hRate : Continuous (fun q : E × (E × E) => rate q.1 q.2) := hb.2.1
  have hPhi : Continuous (fun q : (E × E) × ℝ × (E × E) => Φ q.1.1 q.1.2 q.2.1 q.2.2) := hflow.1
  have ham : StrictMono a := t.property.1
  have haT : ∀ j, a j ≤ (T : ℝ) := by
    intro j
    refine Fin.cases ?_ (fun i => ?_) j
    · simpa [a] using T.coe_nonneg
    · exact (t.property.2 i).le
  have hgrid : Monotone grid := by
    intro i j hij
    induction i using Fin.lastCases with
    | last =>
      have hj : j = Fin.last (n+1) := le_antisymm (Fin.le_last j) hij
      subst j
      exact le_rfl
    | cast i =>
      induction j using Fin.lastCases with
      | last => simpa [grid] using haT i
      | cast j => simpa [grid] using ham.monotone (show i ≤ j from hij)
  have hg0 : grid 0 = 0 := by simp [grid, a]
  have hgT : grid (Fin.last (n+1)) = (T : ℝ) := by simp [grid]
  obtain ⟨Z, _, _, _, _, hlaw⟩ :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.ActualFiniteCountPath.actual_finite_count_path_law
      hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη
  have harc := ((hlaw n T).2.2.2 y r z).2.2.2.2.1
  have heq (j : Fin (n+1)) : EqOn gamma
      (fun s => Φ y r (s - grid j.castSucc) (zAt y r z n T t j))
      (Ioo (grid j.castSucc) (grid j.succ)) := by
    intro s hs
    have hs0 : 0 ≤ s := by
      have := hgrid (show (0 : Fin (n+2)) ≤ j.castSucc from Fin.zero_le _)
      rw [hg0] at this
      exact this.trans hs.1.le
    have hsT : s ≤ (T : ℝ) := by
      have := hgrid (Fin.le_last j.succ)
      rw [hgT] at this
      exact hs.2.le.trans this
    have hclip : min (Real.toNNReal s) T = Real.toNNReal s :=
      min_eq_left (by exact_mod_cast (Real.toNNReal_le_iff_le_coe).2 hsT)
    have hclipcoe : ((min (Real.toNNReal s) T : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) = s := by
      rw [hclip, Real.coe_toNNReal s hs0]
    have hstart : a j ≤ s := by simpa [grid] using hs.1.le
    have hafter : ∀ k : Fin (n+1), j < k → s < a k := by
      intro k hjk
      have hidx : j.succ ≤ k.castSucc := by exact_mod_cast hjk
      exact hs.2.trans_le (by simpa [grid] using hgrid hidx)
    have hh := harc t ⟨min (Real.toNNReal s) T, min_le_right _ _⟩ j
      (by simpa only [hclipcoe] using hstart)
      (by simpa only [hclipcoe] using hafter)
    change gamma s = Φ y r (((min (Real.toNNReal s) T : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) - a j)
      (zAt y r z n T t j) at hh
    simpa only [hclipcoe, grid, Fin.snoc_castSucc] using hh
  obtain ⟨rho, _, _, _, _, hend, _⟩ :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.ActualEndpointTimeReversal.actual_endpoint_time_reversal_laws
      hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη n T
  have hterminal : A = Φ y r ((T : ℝ) - a (Fin.last n)) (zAt y r z n T t (Fin.last n)) :=
    hend y r z t
  have hnext (i : Fin n) : zAt y r z n T t i.succ =
      S r (Φ y r (t.val i - a i.castSucc) (zAt y r z n T t i.castSucc)) := by
    simp only [zAt, Fin.induction_succ]
    rfl
  have hEnd (j : Fin (n+1)) :
      U y (Φ y r (grid j.succ - grid j.castSucc) (zAt y r z n T t j)) = u j.succ := by
    induction j using Fin.lastCases with
    | last =>
      simpa only [Fin.succ_last, grid, u, Fin.snoc_last, Fin.snoc_castSucc] using
        (congrArg (U y) hterminal).symm
    | cast i =>
      simp only [Fin.succ_castSucc, u, Fin.snoc_castSucc]
      rw [hnext]
      simpa only [grid, Fin.succ_castSucc, Fin.snoc_castSucc, a, Fin.cons_succ] using
        (hsU (Φ y r (t.val i - a i.castSucc) (zAt y r z n T t i.castSucc))).symm
  have hstep (j : Fin (n+1)) :
      IntervalIntegrable (fun s => rate r (gamma s)) volume (grid j.castSucc) (grid j.succ) ∧
      IntervalIntegrable (fun s => rate r (R (gamma s))) volume (grid j.castSucc) (grid j.succ) ∧
      (∫ s in grid j.castSucc..grid j.succ, rate r (gamma s)) -
        (∫ s in grid j.castSucc..grid j.succ, rate r (R (gamma s))) = u j.succ - u j.castSucc := by
    let q : ℝ → E × E := fun s => Φ y r (s - grid j.castSucc) (zAt y r z n T t j)
    have harg : Continuous (fun s : ℝ => ((y,r),(s - grid j.castSucc),zAt y r z n T t j)) :=
      continuous_const.prodMk ((continuous_id.sub continuous_const).prodMk continuous_const)
    have hq : Continuous q := hPhi.comp harg
    have hp : Continuous (fun s : ℝ => rate r (q s)) :=
      hRate.comp ((continuous_const (y := r)).prodMk hq)
    have hm : Continuous (fun s : ℝ => rate r (R (q s))) :=
      hRate.comp ((continuous_const (y := r)).prodMk (hq.fst.prodMk hq.snd.neg))
    have hle := hgrid (Fin.castSucc_le_succ j)
    have hip : IntervalIntegrable (fun s => rate r (q s)) volume (grid j.castSucc) (grid j.succ) := hp.intervalIntegrable _ _
    have him : IntervalIntegrable (fun s => rate r (R (q s))) volume (grid j.castSucc) (grid j.succ) := hm.intervalIntegrable _ _
    have hep : EqOn (fun s => rate r (gamma s)) (fun s => rate r (q s)) (Ioo (grid j.castSucc) (grid j.succ)) :=
      fun s hs => congrArg (rate r) (heq j hs)
    have hem : EqOn (fun s => rate r (R (gamma s))) (fun s => rate r (R (q s))) (Ioo (grid j.castSucc) (grid j.succ)) :=
      fun s hs => congrArg (fun w => rate r (R w)) (heq j hs)
    refine ⟨hip.congr_uIoo (by simpa only [uIoo_of_le hle] using hep.symm),
      him.congr_uIoo (by simpa only [uIoo_of_le hle] using hem.symm), ?_⟩
    rw [intervalIntegral.integral_congr_Ioo_of_le hle hep,
      intervalIntegral.integral_congr_Ioo_of_le hle hem, ← intervalIntegral.integral_sub hip him]
    have hd (s : ℝ) : HasDerivAt (fun w => U y (q w))
        (rate r (q s) - rate r (R (q s))) s := by
      have hh : HasDerivAt (fun w => U y (Φ y r w (zAt y r z n T t j)))
          (rate r (q s) - rate r (R (q s))) (s - grid j.castSucc) :=
        (actual_arc_energy hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη y r (zAt y r z n T t j)).1 (s - grid j.castSucc)
      simpa only [Function.comp_def, id_eq, one_smul] using
        hh.scomp s ((hasDerivAt_id s).sub_const (grid j.castSucc))
    rw [intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt (fun s _ => hd s) (hip.sub him)]
    change U y (Φ y r (grid j.succ - grid j.castSucc) (zAt y r z n T t j)) -
      U y (Φ y r (grid j.castSucc - grid j.castSucc) (zAt y r z n T t j)) = _
    rw [hEnd, sub_self, hzero]
    simp only [u, Fin.snoc_castSucc]
  have hf := finite_energy_balance (n+1) grid u
    (fun s => rate r (gamma s)) (fun s => rate r (R (gamma s)))
    (fun j => (hstep j).1) (fun j => (hstep j).2.1) (fun j => (hstep j).2.2)
  have hi : IntervalIntegrable (fun s => rate r (gamma s)) volume 0 (T : ℝ) := by
    simpa only [hg0, hgT] using hf.1
  have hj : IntervalIntegrable (fun s => rate r (R (gamma s))) volume 0 (T : ℝ) := by
    simpa only [hg0, hgT] using hf.2.1
  have henergy : U y A - U y z = Iplus - Iminus := by
    simpa [u, zAt, hg0, hgT] using hf.2.2
  refine ⟨hi, hj, henergy, ?_⟩
  rw [← Real.exp_add, ← Real.exp_add]
  congr 1
  linarith


end

publication_context.statement:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel sigma algebra, including dimension zero. Let V:E->R, alpha,beta>=0 and eta in R. Assume alpha>0, alpha<=beta, V is C2, alpha||v||^2<=D2V(x)[v,v]<=beta||v||^2 for every x,v in E, eta>0 and beta*eta<=1.
For y,r in E put c=y-eta grad V(r), h_r(x)=grad V(x)-grad V(r), R(x,p)=(x,-p),
Phi_(y,r,u)(x,p)=(c+cos(u)(x-c)+sqrt(eta)sin(u)p, -sin(u)/sqrt(eta)(x-c)+cos(u)p),
S_r(x,p)=(x,p-(2<p,h_r(x)>/||h_r(x)||^2)h_r(x)). Real division by zero is zero, so a zero normal gives the identity bounce. Let ell=volume_E tensor volume_E, with canonical Hilbert-space Lebesgue measure.
For every integer n>=0 and horizon T>=0, let Delta_n(T) consist of real tuples 0<t_0<...<t_(n-1)<T. Equivalently, prepending 0 produces a strictly increasing tuple and every entry is less than T. Let Prefix_n(T) be this subtype and m_n,T the comap of Lebesgue measure on R^n under its inclusion. This is unnormalized simplex volume. For n=0 the tuple is empty and its zero-dimensional volume is one; for T=0 and n>0 the subtype is empty.
Write q_0=0 and q_(j+1)=t_j. Starting at z_0=z, define z_(j+1)=S_r(Phi_(y,r,t_j-q_j)(z_j)) for 0<=j<n. Define records K_j=(q_j,z_j), each embedded in the live branch of (R_nonnegative x (E x E)) plus a cemetery symbol. For a general history of n+1 such records, the path reconstruction Psi at s in [0,T] starts from z and visits records in increasing index order: a live record (a,w) replaces the accumulator by Phi_(y,r,s-a)(w) exactly when a<=s; future records and cemetery records leave it unchanged. Here s-a is nonnegative subtraction. Define Gamma_(y,r,z,t)=Psi(K), the actual finite prescribed path; thus its value at an event is the post-bounce value. Let A_(y,r)(z,t)=Gamma_(y,r,z,t)(T).
Define the actual positive-part event rate lambda_r(x,p)=sqrt(eta) max(0,<p,grad V(x)-grad V(r)>), and the target energy U_y(x,p)=V(x)+||x-y||^2/(2 eta)+||p||^2/2. The rate after momentum reversal is lambda_r(R(x,p)); it is evaluated on the same trajectory, not on a reversed-time trajectory.
For every y,r,z,n,T,t as above, extend the actual prescribed path to real s by gamma(s)=Gamma(min(max(s,0),T)), with the argument understood as the nonnegative closed-interval subtype. Put A=Gamma(T), Iplus=integral from 0 to T of lambda_r(gamma(s)) ds, and Iminus=integral from 0 to T of lambda_r(R(gamma(s))) ds, both with real Lebesgue measure. Both integrands are interval integrable. The exact identities are
U_y(A)-U_y(z)=Iplus-Iminus,
exp(-U_y(z)) exp(-Iplus)=exp(-U_y(A)) exp(-Iminus).
All finite event counts n>=0, horizons T>=0, rank-zero spaces and zero reflection normals are included. No positive jump-rate condition is imposed on the prescribed tuple. No measurability, integrability, energy identity or normalizing-constant premise is added to the six source assumptions. The simplex measure m is retained to preserve the existing path interface but is not used by these two scalar identities. The weights here are unnormalized; a common Gibbs normalizer would cancel but existence of the normalized stationary law is a separate obligation.
This is the actual finite prescribed-path energy and Gibbs/survival identity in the Appendix A.1 reversal proof. It does not assert reversed-event density matching, pointwise time reversal at right-continuous jump values, weighted sector preservation, stationary averaging or invariant probability laws, restart/Markovness, hypocoercivity, implementation errors, expected oracle cost, main sampling results or actual-input composition.

sources.scope: No equality of reversed right-continuous jump values, no reversed-event density balance, weighted Theta preservation, stationary averaging/invariance, Markovness, hypocoercivity, errors, expected cost, main result or composition.

assumptions: Finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel E, including rank zero.
alpha,beta>=0; alpha>0; alpha<=beta; V is C2; alpha||v||^2<=D2V(x)[v,v]<=beta||v||^2 for all x,v; eta>0; beta*eta<=1.
Every y,r,z,n>=0,T>=0 and strictly ordered prescribed event tuple; no positive rate or nonzero-normal condition.
Actual Gamma, clamped real-time extension, momentum reversal, positive-part rate and exact U definitions are fixed; both integral finiteness assertions are conclusions.
lesson.statement:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel sigma algebra, including dimension zero. Let V:E->R, alpha,beta>=0 and eta in R. Assume alpha>0, alpha<=beta, V is C2, alpha||v||^2<=D2V(x)[v,v]<=beta||v||^2 for every x,v in E, eta>0 and beta*eta<=1.
For y,r in E put c=y-eta grad V(r), h_r(x)=grad V(x)-grad V(r), R(x,p)=(x,-p),
Phi_(y,r,u)(x,p)=(c+cos(u)(x-c)+sqrt(eta)sin(u)p, -sin(u)/sqrt(eta)(x-c)+cos(u)p),
S_r(x,p)=(x,p-(2<p,h_r(x)>/||h_r(x)||^2)h_r(x)). Real division by zero is zero, so a zero normal gives the identity bounce. Let ell=volume_E tensor volume_E, with canonical Hilbert-space Lebesgue measure.
For every integer n>=0 and horizon T>=0, let Delta_n(T) consist of real tuples 0<t_0<...<t_(n-1)<T. Equivalently, prepending 0 produces a strictly increasing tuple and every entry is less than T. Let Prefix_n(T) be this subtype and m_n,T the comap of Lebesgue measure on R^n under its inclusion. This is unnormalized simplex volume. For n=0 the tuple is empty and its zero-dimensional volume is one; for T=0 and n>0 the subtype is empty.
Write q_0=0 and q_(j+1)=t_j. Starting at z_0=z, define z_(j+1)=S_r(Phi_(y,r,t_j-q_j)(z_j)) for 0<=j<n. Define records K_j=(q_j,z_j), each embedded in the live branch of (R_nonnegative x (E x E)) plus a cemetery symbol. For a general history of n+1 such records, the path reconstruction Psi at s in [0,T] starts from z and visits records in increasing index order: a live record (a,w) replaces the accumulator by Phi_(y,r,s-a)(w) exactly when a<=s; future records and cemetery records leave it unchanged. Here s-a is nonnegative subtraction. Define Gamma_(y,r,z,t)=Psi(K), the actual finite prescribed path; thus its value at an event is the post-bounce value. Let A_(y,r)(z,t)=Gamma_(y,r,z,t)(T).
Define the actual positive-part event rate lambda_r(x,p)=sqrt(eta) max(0,<p,grad V(x)-grad V(r)>), and the target energy U_y(x,p)=V(x)+||x-y||^2/(2 eta)+||p||^2/2. The rate after momentum reversal is lambda_r(R(x,p)); it is evaluated on the same trajectory, not on a reversed-time trajectory.
For every y,r,z,n,T,t as above, extend the actual prescribed path to real s by gamma(s)=Gamma(min(max(s,0),T)), with the argument understood as the nonnegative closed-interval subtype. Put A=Gamma(T), Iplus=integral from 0 to T of lambda_r(gamma(s)) ds, and Iminus=integral from 0 to T of lambda_r(R(gamma(s))) ds, both with real Lebesgue measure. Both integrands are interval integrable. The exact identities are
U_y(A)-U_y(z)=Iplus-Iminus,
exp(-U_y(z)) exp(-Iplus)=exp(-U_y(A)) exp(-Iminus).
All finite event counts n>=0, horizons T>=0, rank-zero spaces and zero reflection normals are included. No positive jump-rate condition is imposed on the prescribed tuple. No measurability, integrability, energy identity or normalizing-constant premise is added to the six source assumptions. The simplex measure m is retained to preserve the existing path interface but is not used by these two scalar identities. The weights here are unnormalized; a common Gibbs normalizer would cancel but existence of the normalized stationary law is a separate obligation.
This is the actual finite prescribed-path energy and Gibbs/survival identity in the Appendix A.1 reversal proof. It does not assert reversed-event density matching, pointwise time reversal at right-continuous jump values, weighted sector preservation, stationary averaging or invariant probability laws, restart/Markovness, hypocoercivity, implementation errors, expected oracle cost, main sampling results or actual-input composition.

steps.title: Differentiate the actual target energy along a flow arc
steps.text: Use the already proved actual ODE xdot=sqrt(eta)p and pdot=-(x-y)/sqrt(eta)-sqrt(eta)grad V(r). The chain rule gives sqrt(eta)<grad V(x),p>+<x-y,p>/sqrt(eta)-<p,x-y>/sqrt(eta)-sqrt(eta)<p,grad V(r)>. The quadratic-force terms cancel exactly. Since max(0,a)-max(0,-a)=a, this derivative equals lambda_r(x,p)-lambda_r(x,-p). Both rates are continuous along every harmonic arc, hence integrable on every finite real interval, and FTC gives the energy increment. The proof includes either orientation and equal interval endpoints.
steps.formula: \frac{d}{ds}U_y(\Phi_s z)=\sqrt\eta\langle p_s,\nabla V(x_s)-\nabla V(r)\rangle=\lambda_r(\Phi_s z)-\lambda_r(R\Phi_s z).

private theorem actual_arc_energy
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    {V : E → ℝ} {α β : ℝ≥0} {η : ℝ}
    (hα : 0 < (α : ℝ)) (hαβ : α ≤ β) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E,
      (α : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ (β : ℝ) * ‖v‖ ^ 2)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hβη : (β : ℝ) * η ≤ 1) :
    let c : E → E → E := fun y r => y - η • gradient V r
    let Φ : E → E → ℝ → (E × E) → (E × E) := fun y r t z =>
      (c y r + Real.cos t • (z.1 - c y r) +
          (Real.sqrt η * Real.sin t) • z.2,
       (-Real.sin t / Real.sqrt η) • (z.1 - c y r) + Real.cos t • z.2)
    let R : E × E → E × E := fun z => (z.1, -z.2)
    let rate : E → E × E → ℝ := fun r z =>
      Real.sqrt η * max 0 (inner ℝ z.2 (gradient V z.1 - gradient V r))
    let U : E → E × E → ℝ := fun y z =>
      V z.1 + ‖z.1 - y‖ ^ 2 / (2 * η) + ‖z.2‖ ^ 2 / 2
    ∀ y r : E, ∀ z : E × E,
      (∀ s : ℝ, HasDerivAt (fun t => U y (Φ y r t z))
        (rate r (Φ y r s z) - rate r (R (Φ y r s z))) s) ∧
      (∀ a b : ℝ,
        IntervalIntegrable (fun s => rate r (Φ y r s z)) volume a b ∧
        IntervalIntegrable (fun s => rate r (R (Φ y r s z))) volume a b ∧
        U y (Φ y r b z) - U y (Φ y r a z) =
          (∫ s in a..b, rate r (Φ y r s z)) -
          (∫ s in a..b, rate r (R (Φ y r s z)))) := by
  intro c Φ R rate U y r z
  letI : CompleteSpace E := FiniteDimensional.complete ℝ E
  have hf := AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.ActualHarmonicFlow.actual_harmonic_flow_laws
    hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη
  rcases hf with ⟨hc, _, _, _, _, ho, _⟩
  have hb := AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.ProximalBPS.ActualBounceRate.actual_bounce_rate_energy_laws
    hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη
  have hrate : Continuous (fun q : E × (E × E) => rate q.1 q.2) := hb.2.1
  have hphi : Continuous (fun t => Φ y r t z) :=
    hc.comp ((continuous_const (y := (y,r))).prodMk
      (continuous_id.prodMk (continuous_const (y := z))))
  have hp : Continuous (fun t => rate r (Φ y r t z)) :=
    hrate.comp (continuous_const.prodMk hphi)
  have hm : Continuous (fun t => rate r (R (Φ y r t z))) :=
    hrate.comp (continuous_const.prodMk (hphi.fst.prodMk hphi.snd.neg))
  have hdiff (q : E × E) : rate r q - rate r (R q) =
      Real.sqrt η * inner ℝ q.2 (gradient V q.1 - gradient V r) := by
    dsimp [rate, R]
    rw [inner_neg_left]
    by_cases h : 0 ≤ inner ℝ q.2 (gradient V q.1 - gradient V r)
    · rw [max_eq_right h, max_eq_left (neg_nonpos.mpr h)]
      ring
    · rw [max_eq_left (le_of_not_ge h), max_eq_right (neg_nonneg.mpr (le_of_not_ge h))]
      ring
  have hd (s : ℝ) : HasDerivAt (fun t => U y (Φ y r t z))
      (rate r (Φ y r s z) - rate r (R (Φ y r s z))) s := by
    obtain ⟨hx, hv⟩ := ho y r s z
    have hx' : HasDerivAt (fun t => (Φ y r t z).1) (Real.sqrt η • (Φ y r s z).2) s := hx
    have hv' : HasDerivAt (fun t => (Φ y r t z).2)
        (-(Real.sqrt η)⁻¹ • ((Φ y r s z).1 - y) - Real.sqrt η • gradient V r) s := hv
    have hVd := ((hV.differentiable (by norm_num)).differentiableAt.hasGradientAt.hasFDerivAt).comp_hasDerivAt s hx'
    have hd0 := (hVd.add ((hx'.sub_const y).norm_sq.div_const (2 * η))).add

    simp only [InnerProductSpace.toDual_apply_apply, real_inner_smul_right, real_inner_smul_left,
      inner_sub_right, inner_sub_left, real_inner_comm]

steps.title: Telescope the finite energy grid
steps.text: For each adjacent grid interval assume, only inside this private lemma, that f and g are integrable and their integral difference is u_(j+1)-u_j. The empty grid has zero integral and zero energy increment. Append one interval: oriented interval additivity gives both integrals on the enlarged interval, and the intermediate energy cancels. Induction therefore yields the endpoint energy difference. The public proof below supplies all these local facts from the actual trajectory; this helper introduces no public premise.
steps.lean:
private theorem finite_energy_balance (n : ℕ) (a u : Fin (n+1) → ℝ)
    (f g : ℝ → ℝ)
    (hf : ∀ j : Fin n, IntervalIntegrable f volume (a j.castSucc) (a j.succ))
    (hg : ∀ j : Fin n, IntervalIntegrable g volume (a j.castSucc) (a j.succ))
    (hstep : ∀ j : Fin n,
      (∫ s in a j.castSucc..a j.succ, f s) -
        (∫ s in a j.castSucc..a j.succ, g s) = u j.succ - u j.castSucc) :
    IntervalIntegrable f volume (a 0) (a (Fin.last n)) ∧
    IntervalIntegrable g volume (a 0) (a (Fin.last n)) ∧
    u (Fin.last n) - u 0 =
      (∫ s in a 0..a (Fin.last n), f s) -
        (∫ s in a 0..a (Fin.last n), g s) := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
    have hh := ih (fun i => a i.castSucc) (fun i => u i.castSucc)
      (fun j => hf j.castSucc) (fun j => hg j.castSucc)
      (fun j => by simpa only [Fin.succ_castSucc] using hstep j.castSucc)
    have hfl := hf (Fin.last n)
    have hgl := hg (Fin.last n)
    have hs := hstep (Fin.last n)
    refine ⟨hh.1.trans hfl, hh.2.1.trans hgl, ?_⟩
    have hfi := intervalIntegral.integral_add_adjacent_intervals hh.1 hfl
    have hgi := intervalIntegral.integral_add_adjacent_intervals hh.2.1 hgl
    simp only [Fin.succ_last, Fin.castSucc_zero] at hh hs hfi hgi
    linarith [hh.2.2]

steps.title: Preserve target energy at every actual bounce
steps.text: The actual reflection preserves position and momentum norm, including a zero normal. Thus V(x), the quadratic position term and the kinetic term are all unchanged by S_r. Reuse the actual flow initial identity and the continuity of the actual rate and flow. The energy grid consists of U evaluated at the post-bounce states, with the final entry U(A). These are literal actual states, not supplied witnesses.

steps.title: Identify each open arc of the actual clamped path
steps.text: Prepend zero to the strictly ordered event times and append T to form a monotone grid. On the open jth interval, the real-time clamp equals s. Earlier history records have already occurred and later records are strictly in the future. Apply the verified actual finite-count path law to obtain gamma(s)=Phi_(s-a_j)(z_j). Only open-interval equality is used, so right-continuous values at event times are not confused with incoming states; a finite set of endpoints does not affect the Lebesgue integrals.

# Anonymous theorem reconstruction

Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space, equipped with its normed additive group structure and a measurable-space structure whose measurable sets are the Borel sets. Let V : E → ℝ be twice continuously Fréchet differentiable. Let α, β be nonnegative real numbers and η a real number. Assume

- α > 0 and α ≤ β;
- for every x, v ∈ E, α ‖v‖² ≤ D²V(x)[v,v] ≤ β ‖v‖²;
- η > 0 and βη ≤ 1.

Here D²V(x)[v,v] means exactly (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v, and ∇V denotes the real Hilbert gradient. The occurrences of α and β in real expressions use their coercions to ℝ.

For y, r ∈ E define c(y,r) = y − η ∇V(r). For any real u and phase-space point (q,p) ∈ E × E define

Φ(y,r,u,(q,p)) = (c(y,r) + cos(u)(q − c(y,r)) + √η sin(u) p, −sin(u)/√η (q − c(y,r)) + cos(u) p).

Scalar multiplication here is real scalar multiplication on E. Put d_r(q) = ∇V(q) − ∇V(r), and define

S_r(q,p) = (q, p − [2 ⟨p,d_r(q)⟩ / ‖d_r(q)‖²] d_r(q)).

Division uses Lean real division: a division by zero is zero. In particular S_r(q,p) = (q,p) when d_r(q) = 0; there is no nonzero-gradient-difference assumption.

Choose arbitrarily y, r ∈ E, an initial phase-space point z ∈ E × E, an integer n ≥ 0, a nonnegative real horizon T, and n real times τ₁,…,τₙ satisfying

0 < τ₁ < ⋯ < τₙ < T.

When n = 0 this condition is empty. Set τ₀ = 0 and Z₀ = z. Recursively, for j = 1,…,n, set

Zⱼ = S_r(Φ(y,r,τⱼ − τⱼ₋₁,Zⱼ₋₁)).

Thus Zⱼ is the state after applying S_r at time τⱼ. This indexing is a mathematical reindexing of the input's zero-based Fin n coordinates.

For 0 ≤ s ≤ T, let k(s) be the largest index j ∈ {0,…,n} such that τⱼ ≤ s, and define

Γ(s) = Φ(y,r,s − τₖ₍ₛ₎,Zₖ₍ₛ₎).

The index exists because τ₀ = 0. This is exactly the stated increasing-index fold: every live record whose time is at most s overwrites the accumulated value with its own flow value, so the last eligible record supplies the result. At each listed time τⱼ the path takes the post-reflection state Zⱼ. There is no reflection scheduled at T. Extend the path to every real s by

γ(s) = Γ(min(max(s,0),T)),

and set A = Γ(T). Define velocity reversal, the nonnegative rate, and the energy by

R(q,p) = (q,−p),
λ_r(q,p) = √η max(0, ⟨p,∇V(q) − ∇V(r)⟩),
U_y(q,p) = V(q) + ‖q − y‖²/(2η) + ‖p‖²/2.

Let

I₊ = ∫₀ᵀ λ_r(γ(s)) ds,
I₋ = ∫₀ᵀ λ_r(R(γ(s))) ds,

where ds is Lebesgue measure on ℝ and both expressions are Lean's interval integrals, with their usual signed orientation. Since T is nonnegative, the endpoints have nonnegative orientation.

The theorem asserts, for every choice above, all four statements simultaneously:

1. s ↦ λ_r(γ(s)) is interval-integrable with respect to Lebesgue measure between 0 and T.
2. s ↦ λ_r(R(γ(s))) is interval-integrable with respect to Lebesgue measure between 0 and T.
3. U_y(A) − U_y(z) = I₊ − I₋.
4. exp(−U_y(z)) exp(−I₊) = exp(−U_y(A)) exp(−I₋).

## Exact auxiliary objects and scope

The time-prefix set Δ(n,T) consists of t : Fin n → ℝ such that the function obtained by prepending 0 is strictly increasing and every coordinate is strictly less than T. Prefix(n,T) is the subtype of such t. Its membership proof is part of its type; the theorem quantifies over every element of that subtype, not almost every element.

The anonymous declaration also defines Rec = (ℝ≥0 × (E × E)) ⊕ Unit and Hist(n) = Fin(n+1) → Rec. A left summand is a time/state record, and the Unit right summand is the cemetery branch. The canonical history K has the n+1 live records (τⱼ,Zⱼ), with times converted by Real.toNNReal; all these times are already nonnegative. K never uses a cemetery record.

Path(T) is the full function type {s : ℝ≥0 | s ≤ T} → E × E. For a general Hist(n), Ψ evaluates a path by starting its fold at z, traversing all n+1 records in increasing index order, ignoring cemetery records and records with time greater than s, and overwriting the accumulator with Φ(y,r,s−a,state) at each eligible live record (a,state). The subtraction in this definition is nonnegative-real truncated subtraction, then coerced to ℝ; eligibility a ≤ s makes it ordinary elapsed time. No sortedness is required for the definition of Ψ on arbitrary histories. The theorem only applies Ψ to the canonical K above, producing Γ. It asserts no general-history result.

The local measure m(n,T) is Measure.comap of the subtype-value map Prefix(n,T) → (Fin n → ℝ), applied to volume on the real coordinate-function space. This is the exact unnormalized subtype measure specified by the input. It is unused in the conclusion and supplies no measure-theoretic hypothesis or probabilistic quantifier.

All displayed constructions are local definitions inside the theorem. They depend on the fixed E, V, and η where those parameters occur. α and β constrain V and η through the hypotheses, but no local flow, reflection, path, rate, or energy formula contains α or β explicitly. The center and flow depend on y and r; reflection and rate depend on r; energy depends on y; the canonical trajectory depends on y,r,z,n,T,t. No constants are existentially quantified, and there is no unspecified constant or uniformity convention.

The conclusions are deterministic statements for every finite prescribed prefix. They do not assert a distribution of prefixes, a random event count, path sampling, invariance of a probability measure, normalization of an exponential density, reversibility of a path law, or a relation to a separately constructed reversed trajectory. R in I₋ reverses the velocity at the same γ(s), without changing the time argument.

If n = 0 then Γ(s) = Φ(y,r,s,z) on [0,T]. If T = 0 then Prefix(n,T) is empty for n > 0, so those quantifications are vacuous; for n = 0 the trajectory endpoint is z and both integrals vanish. The space E is not required to have positive dimension. The path is not asserted continuous at reflection times; the theorem asserts interval integrability of the two scalar rate functions.

## Input limitations

Only the anonymous Lean statement and its approved definition context were inspected. The supplied metadata reports compilation, but this decoding performs no independent compilation or proof inspection. No original source text, source identity, or source-equivalence verdict is used or asserted. There is no unresolved ambiguity in the decoded quantifier or construction scopes; the input's exact Measure.comap convention is retained without replacing it by a probability law.
